pairs.subject: accessibility
pairs.evidence: app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.a11y.test.ts:12 The glyph's only accessibility gate pattern-matches the renderer's source text rather than asserting the computed role/name or the absence from the tree on rendered output. That is the attribute-correlate check gate-sees-target rules out, even though the primitive itself names and hides correctly.

techniques.evidence: app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.a11y.test.ts:12 The a11y guard is a regex over MotionizedGlyph.tsx, not a query by role and name on rendered output, so a refactor that keeps the spread text but changes what reaches the accessibility tree still passes. The reduced-motion tests (glyphMotionCss.test.ts) do assert real derived CSS output.

app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:186 Decorative by default (aria-hidden, so it is not voiced twice beside its heading). With a label it becomes a named img. One expression decides both states, and the label comes from the consumer's translated string.
app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:73 The naming and hiding contract lives once, inside the shared renderer every glyph consumer passes through, rather than at each call site.

app/_components/glyph/glyphMotionCss.ts:51 Under prefers-reduced-motion each preset's declared `reduced` field is derived into the stylesheet. Entrances cross-fade or settle instantly with opacity restored (replaced, not removed). Ambient loops are dropped, and the replay observer is never armed (MotionizedGlyph.tsx:140). Both reads use the OS query through the shared useReducedMotion hook and the CSS media block; there is no in-app override.
app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:175 The glyph is a non-interactive svg with no tabIndex or handlers, so it has no keyboard model to own.

pairs.registryProposal: a11y-verification assumes a component test layer that can render and query by role. In a repo whose unit runner (node:test) has no DOM, teams fall back to source-regex guards and justify them. The technique could say explicitly whether a source guard counts as a partial layer-2 substitute or as a gate-sees-target violation, and name the cheapest compliant alternative (for example, server-rendering the primitive to markup and asserting attributes per branch).
